inconsistencies: Logging trio solves the same problem three ways: #34038 (-trace + logging RPC), #35355 (superset of #34038 plus atomic level checks), #35387 (ryanofsky's alternative loglevel RPC, flagged by stickies-v as competing with #34038). A single design decision should precede any of them; review #34038 first as the self-contained non-draft version, then compare #35387, then #35355.

#36384 and #34950 both migrate RPC argument parsing to self.Arg<>(); #36384 covers node and wallet RPCs broadly and likely subsumes the generatetoaddress case in #34950. Review #36384 first; #34950 may become redundant.

Large HTTP-server cluster follows the #35182 rewrite and touches the same files: #36187, #36355, #36354, #36259, #36204, #36200, #35780, plus follow-up refactors #36124 and #36159. The security/correctness fixes should land before the refactors (#36124 is explicitly a follow-up to the merged #35829), or the refactors will need rebasing and re-review.

#36332 (MuSig2 metadata injected before relevance check) and #35370 (strip existing key-origin/xpub metadata) both concern unwanted derivation data in PSBTs returned by processing RPCs; #36332 is the defect and should be reviewed first, #35370 is the opt-in control.

#27260 and #36273 are both about misleading RPC error text (address network prefix vs. raw-tx decode hints). #27260 is the broader user-facing case; if only one gets attention it should be that one, and the two should use consistent message style.

#33904 and #35909 are both REST-parity gaps tracked under existing issues (#33808, #35897) and touch REST query-parameter parsing; #35909 also deduplicates boolean query-param handling, so merging it first reduces conflict for #33904.

Three deprecation PRs (#35433 replaceable, #36387 encryptwallet, #36488 confTarget) all stage removals behind -deprecatedrpc in the same cycle; they are independent in code but should be decided together so callers face one migration wave.
#10102 states a dependency on #29409 and unblocks #19460/#19461; its rpc-category content is only internal request dispatch, so its real weight lives in the process-separation project, not here.
#36002 builds on index key-format changes already merged in #35531 — no conflict, but reviewers should confirm that prerequisite is in place.
result.notes: The top of this category is dominated by fallout from the HTTP server rewrite plus two authentication/exposure issues; those are the only items where another release cycle of delay is clearly harmful. Per the category's compatibility-first rule, PRs that return silently wrong or incomplete data to existing callers (#35837, #36385, #35728, #36343) were kept at or above new-interface work, and new RPCs or fields without a cited external consumer (#31672, #29418, #33904, #32468) were placed at the bottom of P3 even when well motivated internally.
